nodes.title: SG-2.4 Manifest loader checks references and falls back without crashing
nodes.body:
Context: game/src/assets/loaders/manifestLoader.ts has loadManifestFile, which validates the manifest and checks that each asset file exists on disk. It does not check that scene/object asset refs point at manifest ids, and it has no fallback: any missing file makes the whole load fail with ok:false. Desired behavior: every manifest reference is verified, missing assets are reported by id, and the loader returns a usable manifest plus a fallback asset instead of failing or throwing. Why: missing art must degrade gracefully, never crash the game.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a scene ref that is not a manifest id, when references are checked, then the dangling ref is reported by name.
- Given a manifest asset whose file is missing, when loaded with fallback, then the missing asset is reported and the load still returns a manifest without throwing.
- Given an unreadable or malformed manifest, when loaded with fallback, then an empty manifest and the error are returned without throwing.


## Scope
- In scope: game/src/assets/loaders/manifestLoader.ts
- In scope: reference check and fallback result
- Out of scope: Phaser scene wiring
- Out of scope: new art assets
- Out of scope: changes to the manifest schema
- Preserve: loadManifestFile behavior and its existing tests
- Preserve: parseManifest and schema


## Technical constraints
- TypeScript, zod schema already in game/src/assets/manifest
- Loader must never throw
- Use node fs only inside the loader, as today


## Definition of done
- Both requirements implemented and verified by unit tests


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Loader reports object and scene asset refs that are not manifest ids
nodes.body:
Context: bedroom.yaml objects carry an asset string that must equal a manifest asset id, but only a test checks this today. Desired behavior: an exported loader helper takes the manifest and a list of refs and returns an issue for each ref that has no matching manifest id. Expected result: callers can validate content against the manifest at load time. Why: a typo in content must be reported, not crash rendering.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given refs ['a','ghost'] and a manifest with only id 'a', when checkAssetRefs runs, then one issue is returned naming 'ghost'.
- Given all refs match manifest ids, when checkAssetRefs runs, then an empty list is returned.
- Given an empty refs list, when checkAssetRefs runs, then an empty list is returned and nothing throws.


## Scope
- In scope: checkAssetRefs helper in manifestLoader.ts
- Out of scope: reading yaml scene files in the loader
- Preserve: existing loader exports


## Technical constraints
- Reuse ManifestIssue type from ../manifest


## Definition of done
- checkAssetRefs exported and covered by unit tests


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Loader reports missing asset files and falls back without crashing
nodes.body:
Context: loadManifestFile returns ok:false when any file is missing, giving callers nothing to render. Desired behavior: a new loadManifestWithFallback returns { manifest, missing, errors, fallbackAssetId } where manifest contains only assets whose files exist, missing lists absent assets, and an unreadable or invalid manifest yields an empty manifest with errors. Expected result: the game keeps running with a fallback asset id for anything missing. Why: no crash on missing art.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given one existing and one missing asset file, when loadManifestWithFallback runs, then manifest holds only the existing asset and missing names the other id and path.
- Given a nonexistent manifest file, when it runs, then it returns an empty assets list and one error, and does not throw.
- Given all files exist, when it runs, then missing is empty and the result equals the full manifest.


## Scope
- In scope: loadManifestWithFallback and FALLBACK_ASSET_ID in manifestLoader.ts
- Out of scope: creating a real fallback image
- Out of scope: Phaser texture generation
- Preserve: loadManifestFile signature and behavior


## Technical constraints
- Must never throw
- Build on loadManifestFile and parseManifest


## Definition of done
- loadManifestWithFallback exported and covered by unit tests


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: Act: Add loadManifestWithFallback to the manifest loader
nodes.body:
Add a never-throwing loader that keeps existing assets, reports missing ones and returns an empty manifest on unreadable or invalid input.

## Acceptance criteria
- Missing files are listed and dropped from the manifest
- Unreadable manifest yields empty assets plus errors


## Scope
- In scope: game/src/assets/loaders/manifestLoader.ts
- Out of scope: tests
- Preserve: loadManifestFile


## Technical constraints
- No throwing
- Code path: `game/src/assets/loaders/manifestLoader.ts`

- Function exported and typechecks


## Clarifying questions
- None
nodes.description: Add a never-throwing loader that keeps existing assets, reports missing ones and returns an empty manifest on unreadable or invalid input.
acceptance_criteria: Missing files are listed and dropped from the manifest
Unreadable manifest yields empty assets plus errors

steps.action: Export const FALLBACK_ASSET_ID = 'fallback:missing' and type FallbackLoadResult = { manifest: AssetManifest; missing: { id: string; path: string }[]; errors: ManifestIssue[]; fallbackAssetId: string }.

Export loadManifestWithFallback(manifestPath, assetsRoot): FallbackLoadResult. Read and JSON.parse in try/catch; on failure or parseManifest !ok return manifest {version:1, assets:[]}, errors set, missing []. Otherwise split parsed.data.assets by existsSync(join(assetsRoot, asset.path)); keep existing ones in manifest, push the rest to missing; errors []. Always set fallbackAssetId: FALLBACK_ASSET_ID.
steps.expected: Function returns without throwing for every input.
